p: are not hidden from the Almighty: Thus Job speaks in his passions, and after the judgment of the flesh: that is, that he does not see the things that are done at times, nor yet has a peculiar care over all, because he does not punish the wicked or avenge the godly.
days: When he punishes the wicked and rewards the good.
together: And for cruelty and oppression dare not show their faces.
rising betimes for a prey: That is, spares diligence.
yieldeth food for them and for: He and his live by robbing and murdering.
his corn in the field: Meaning the poor man's.
vintage of the wicked: Signifying that one wicked man will not spoil another, but for necessity.
and embrace the rock for want: The poor are driven by the wicked into the rock and holes where they cannot lie dry for the rain.
from the breast: That is, they so pillage and plunder the poor widow that she cannot sustain herself that she may be able to nurse her baby.
within their walls: In such places which are appointed for that purpose; meaning, that those who labour for the wicked, are pined for hunger.
groan from out of the city: For the great oppression and extortion.
layeth not folly to them: Cry out and call for vengeance.
light: That is, God's word, because they are reproved by it.
adulterer waiteth for the twilight: By these particular vices and the licence of it, he would prove that God did not punish the wicked and reward the just.
waters: He flees to the waters for his succour.
portion is cursed in the earth: They think that all the world is bent against them and dare not go by the highway.
have sinned: As the dry ground is never full with waters, so will they never cease sinning till they come to the grave.
The womb shall forget him: Though God tolerates the wicked for a time, yet their end will be vile destruction, and in this point Job commits to himself and shows his confidence.
evil entreateth the barren that beareth: He shows why the wicked will not be lamented, because he did not pity others.
mighty with his power: He declares that after the wicked have destroyed the weakest, they will do the same to the stranger, and therefore are justly punished by God's judgments.
so now: That is, contrary to your reasoning no man can give perfect reasons for God's judgments, let me be reproved.
